published_prior_art.cite: BenaychGeorgesNadakuditi2012 gives fixed-spike singular-value/vector limits, not a coefficient-indexed uniform profiled argmin.
CardosoFermanFernandes2026 identifies a strong heterogeneous-factor absorption endpoint, not the stated local subcritical region.
BenaychGeorgesNadakuditi2012 and BloemendalVirag2013 do not classify global minima of a coefficient-indexed rectangular spectral potential.
CardosoFermanFernandes2026 proves the strong-factor bad-control endpoint; no verified paper gives this local selection/phase law.
ArmstrongWeidnerZeleneev2026 studies weak-factor-robust inference and conventional-CI distortion, not this treatment-supported local absorption region.
BaiNg2021 gives tall-wide imputation and ATT normal theory, not simultaneous uniform validity along this local full-sample selection experiment.
Bai2009 supplies the homogeneous strong-factor IFE benchmark; the proposition is chiefly a necessary reduction of the new profile.

novelty_flags.label: full-sample/masked comparison
novelty_flags.one_line: The claimed enterprise-zone implication rests on exact orthogonality to latent loadings and factors, while the core itself admits that this makes the raw treated-post mean unbiased; it supplies no independently natural submodel or observable implementation establishing the benchmark's applied relevance.

soundness_flags.label: def:full-wald and def:masked-wald
soundness_flags.one_line: Both residual scale estimators are only called “conventional” or “computed from” residuals, with no formula, degrees-of-freedom convention, or selection rule; CI_F and CI_M therefore are not uniquely defined.

soundness_flags.label: thm:absorption-law / xsel
soundness_flags.one_line: xsel is declared only as an unspecified random element but is used as xsel(eta,h); at ties the OEQ itself permits slow nuisance drift, so the claimed limit law lacks its required drift-path and randomness inputs.

soundness_flags.label: def:masked-estimator and thm:masked-coverage
soundness_flags.one_line: “Admissible” C_A,C_B is not defined or linked to a normalized true factorization, so the constrained fitting class need not contain the baseline matrix over which coverage is claimed.

soundness_flags.label: ass:untreated-loading-gram and ass:untreated-gram-envelope
soundness_flags.one_line: M_d=I-ddᵀ/n_1 projects off one treatment-vector direction; it is not the selector onto untreated units, so these conditions do not impose the advertised tall-block loading condition needed by the masked fit.

soundness_flags.label: ass:pre-factor-gram and ass:pre-gram-envelope
soundness_flags.one_line: M_q=I-qqᵀ/t_1 is not the selector onto pre-treatment periods, so these conditions do not impose the advertised wide-block factor condition for the observed-cell estimator.

soundness_flags.label: ass:loading-row-bound
soundness_flags.one_line: Bai2009 Assumption B uses bounded fourth moments and a Gram limit, not the deterministic uniform maximum-row loading bound tagged as its standard condition.

soundness_flags.label: ass:factor-row-bound
soundness_flags.one_line: Bai2009 Assumption B uses a fourth-moment condition for factors, not the stated deterministic max_t row bound.

soundness_flags.label: ass:bounded-unit-scores
soundness_flags.one_line: The Bai2009 loading condition concerns baseline factor loadings, not treatment-effect score arrays a; the stated citation does not support this tagged standard condition.

soundness_flags.label: ass:bounded-time-scores
soundness_flags.one_line: The Bai2009 factor condition concerns baseline factors, not treatment-effect score arrays b; the stated citation does not support this tagged standard condition.

soundness_flags.label: ass:left-support-orthogonality
soundness_flags.one_line: Exact orthogonality of a binary treatment assignment to latent baseline loadings is not operationally justified by “measured baseline factor loadings.”

soundness_flags.label: ass:left-score-orthogonality
soundness_flags.one_line: Exact orthogonality of treatment-supported heterogeneous scores to latent loadings is an instrumental oracle restriction without a credible applied construction.

soundness_flags.label: ass:right-support-orthogonality
soundness_flags.one_line: A fixed post-period indicator cannot generally be selected exactly orthogonal to unobserved common factors; the asserted residualized-event-window justification does not establish this.

soundness_flags.label: ass:right-score-orthogonality
soundness_flags.one_line: Exact orthogonality of post-period response scores to latent common factors is an unverified oracle restriction rather than a demonstrated realistic regime.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Assumption B specifies bounded fourth moments for factors and loadings together with convergence of T⁻¹FᵀF and N⁻¹ΛᵀΛ; it does not state deterministic maximum-row bounds.
The limiting distribution is invariant to non-underestimated fitted rank under its assumptions, which explicitly rule out low-rank regressors.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of Multivariate Analysis 111, 2012 journal PDF
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Finite-rank rectangular perturbations have an outlier and singular-vector phase transition governed by the fixed perturbation singular values.
The paper studies heterogeneous-treatment IFE bad controls and states that estimators excluding treated post-treatment outcomes from factor estimation avoid that problem.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of Political Economy 134(8), published online 26 June 2026
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper develops bias-aware minimax-linear estimates and uniformly valid confidence intervals for weak interactive factors.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of the American Statistical Association 116(536), 2021
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The published article uses factors from a tall block and re-rotated loadings from a wide block for imputation and establishes ATT normal theory.
The paper studies a growing fitted factor count and obtains a conditional-variance-weighted treatment-effect estimand.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace exact latent-space orthogonality with an observable residualization/design condition, or explicitly prove that the phase law persists under quantified approximate orthogonality while separating ordinary baseline-confounding bias from absorption.

Define both residual variance estimators, the singular-subspace tie rule, and xsel as a measurable functional of the full nuisance-drift path and limiting noise process; otherwise restrict all limit claims to stable singleton geometries.

Replace M_d and M_q in masked-block identification assumptions with selector-matrix conditions for controls and pre-periods, and state factor-bound constants that make the true normalized factorization feasible.

Retag the four maximum-score/factor bounds as novel sufficient regularity conditions with credible applications, or replace them with the moment conditions actually supplied by Bai2009 and rework the uniform arguments.

recommended_next_step: Revise the masked-block conditions and oracle geometry first, then make the two Wald objects and tie-selection limit fully specified before advancing to Stage 0.
